ideas.title: A whale swims through the ground
ideas.critique: A big unseen thing passing under the surface is a known picture, and the tail breaking out of the turf will be a canned set-piece. The strong part is ground that moves like a medium: a travelling heave that carries real props, trees and bodies, with friends sliding down its front. The island has never had that. If the bulge is just a vertex offset and the props are not really thrown by it, it reads as a shader.

ideas.title: Somebody is looking in
ideas.critique: This is round 2's suitcase island again, minus the tiny copy. What is left is a giant face asset in the sky dimming the sun, which makes it the fourth sun/light change in a row, and a scripted wave on the beach. Calling the sun's eclipse a blink is the one nice touch. It is a one-shot cutscene with nothing to play or watch twice.

ideas.title: Fished out of the sea
ideas.critique: Moving the whole island as one body is the seesaw and drift recipe, and lifting and dropping it is rearranging the island with nothing new to play with. The water sheeting off the underside and a splash wave ringing to the horizon would be new if it is a real Maelstrom fluid sim. If it is just a transform on a curve with a painted splash, this is a cutscene.

ideas.title: Heavy hearts
ideas.critique: Turning feelings into weight is a familiar metaphor, and 'cheering up lifts you' is the obvious ending. What is strong is that real mood values change bodies and leave dents in the ground, and the friends react to each other physically by pulling and holding hands, which is the creature-to-creature interaction the goals want. It falls flat if the rescues are scripted rather than set off by a friend actually sinking.

ideas.title: Marbles with the stars
ideas.critique: Glowing balls falling from the sky and rolling across the grass is Football with the sun again, now made plural, and this would be the fifth light-on-the-meadow post. The new step is that it can be played: flicking, collisions and the winner keeping a star. That only helps if the marble physics and the player's flick are real, and the trace has to show light sliding across faces, not just glowing dots.
